content.title: Object-by-Object Rewrite | Local Conversions to a Whole-Environment Payoff
content.summary: Hold one continuous first-person view of a real environment while a visible tool selects objects at increasing scales. Convert only the selected object and preserve its exact location; after at least three local proofs, apply the same established rule once to an entire environmental region.

quick_start.input_format: Continuous real environment + visible selection tool + at least three local object conversions + in-place spatial registration + one whole-environment conversion
quick_start.recommended_input: In an original precision cleanroom, a gloved technician raises a compact amber inspection emitter and aligns it with a graphite valve. White wall panels, the floor grid, and conveyor equipment remain real. When the beam touches a robot chassis, only the robot becomes a layered schematic at the same location; its wheels, route, and surrounding machines remain spatially registered. The beam then reaches the ceiling grid, and the same conversion boundary expands downward until ceiling, machinery, and floor form one cyan cleanroom cutaway, with the emitter still visible in the foreground.
required_anchors: Establish one continuous real environment and one visible selection tool.
Align the tool with one object before each local conversion.
Repeat the rule across at least three materially different object scales while keeping geography traceable.
Apply the established rule once to a whole environmental region and hold the boundary.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Hold one continuous first-person view of a real environment while a visible tool selects objects at increasing scales. Convert only the selected object and preserve its exact location; after at least three local proofs, apply the same established rule once to an entire environmental region.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Keep one real environment and one visible selection tool continuous, align the tool with a sequence of distinct objects, and convert only the selected object into a new visual medium while preserving its spatial anchor and the rest of the world. Repeat across increasing scales, then reserve one final gesture that applies the already-proven conversion rule to a complete environmental region.

invariants.rule: Establish one continuous real environment and one visible selection tool.
invariants.purpose: Defines the baseline and causal agent.
invariants.ablation_failure: An unexplained transformed opening has no conversion rule.

invariants.rule: Align the tool with one object before each local conversion.
invariants.purpose: Makes every change attributable and readable.
invariants.ablation_failure: Objects changing before selection become random VFX.

invariants.rule: Convert only the selected object while preserving its location and surrounding reality.
invariants.ablation_failure: Changing the whole frame on every beat removes local evidence.

invariants.rule: Repeat the rule across at least three materially different object scales while keeping geography traceable.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeated copies of one object do not test the rule.

invariants.rule: Apply the established rule once to a whole environmental region and hold the boundary.
invariants.ablation_failure: Another local conversion cannot close the escalation.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source black marker and bare hand
the source Korean city, bus shelter, elevated train and green bus
the source illustrated train, pigeon, orange cat and seated anime girl
the source smiling sun and cloud sky
the AIGC watermark and exact object order

instantiations.concept: In an original cleanroom, a technician uses an amber inspection beam to select a valve, a conveyor robot and a pressure window. Each selected object alone becomes a transparent exploded blueprint at the same location; the final beam reaches the ceiling grid and converts the whole room into one held schematic cutaway.

instantiations.concept: In tactile stop-motion pottery, a small copper stamp touches a cup, a kiln cart and a wall vent; each becomes a layered paper cross-section while the clay studio stays intact. The last stamp touches the floor grid and the entire workshop becomes a folded instructional model.
